To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the virtual community members are motivated by the community’s social, informational and personal benefits, and these factors have a positive impact on the user satisfaction with the virtual community.

the following variables are significant to member need satisfaction: (1) community member’s perception of the community as an information source, (2) community member’s satisfaction with the quality and quantity of information, (3) the member’s perception of community’s ability to meet their needs, and (4) the member’s satisfaction with community’s ability to facilitate interaction.

the more a member perceives that the community is a good source for information, the more he or she is willing to participate and contribute to the community, the more the member will perceive that the community provides him or her with a sense of belonging, and the more the member is likely to perceive that the community is providing him or her with an opportunity to learn and to share knowledge with other community members, all of which will lead to the member's perception of higher satisfaction with the community.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the uses of virtual communities, and the gratifications that users derive from their uses of virtual communities.
the following issues: (1) What factors motivate users to participate in the virtual community?
the following questions: What are the needs of virtual community members?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the uses and gratifications framework can be applied in a virtual community environment.
a virtual community of users and members is successful if the users are satisfied with the community.
virtual community members are more motivated and satisfied if they perceive the virtual community as a source of information and knowledge and as a social environment for interaction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the uses and gratifications theory can be applied in the virtual environment.
the more members use the virtual community, the more satisfied they are.
we found that the uses and gratifications framework could be applied to virtual community environment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the uses and gratifications theory can be used in virtual communities as a tool to measure user needs and satisfaction.
we have developed an initial set of scales that can be used to measure the success of a virtual community.
the uses and gratifications approach can provide an effective framework to understand virtual community success.
